_comment: C libraries that wheels link into their native modules, reviewed by hand (static-licenses.mjs adds each to the dist's record with its text). Keys are normalized distribution names. `detect` is a regular expression whose first group reads the library's version from the binary; without it, `version` says what is known. `text` is where the licence text comes from ({version} is filled in). A distribution listed here needs a record for its exact version or the stage fails. `kind` names what is bundled when it is not a C library linked into a module (THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES prints it).

cryptography.name: OpenSSL
cryptography.why: cryptography's wheels link OpenSSL into hazmat/bindings/_rust (its version string is in the binary); the wheel's own LICENSE does not name it

cffi.name: libffi
cffi.why: _cffi_backend exports ffi_prep_cif and loads no libffi: libffi is linked in; cffi's LICENSE does not name it

ruamel-yaml-clib.name: libyaml
ruamel-yaml-clib.why: _ruamel_yaml exports libyaml's yaml_* functions from the copy ruamel.yaml.clib compiles in; its LICENSE names only ruamel

pywinpty.name: winpty
pywinpty.why: pywinpty's Windows wheel ships rprichard/winpty as winpty/winpty.dll and winpty/winpty-agent.exe (winpty-agent prints "winpty version 0.4.3"); pywinpty's LICENSE.txt names only Spyder IDE

pywinpty.name: Windows Terminal OpenConsole and ConPTY
pywinpty.version: 1.25.2609.30003 (the binaries' file version; text from the v1.25.2733.0 release tag)
pywinpty.why: pywinpty's Windows wheel ships microsoft/terminal's winpty/OpenConsole.exe and winpty/conpty.dll (ProductName "Windows Terminal", Microsoft Corporation); pywinpty's LICENSE.txt does not name them
